title: All Paths From Source to Target
summary: Given a directed acyclic graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, find all possible paths from node 0 to node n-1 and return them in any order.
statement: Given a directed acyclic graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, find all possible paths from node 0 to node n-1 and return them in any order. The graph is represented such that graph[i] contains a list of all nodes that can be reached from node i.
constraints: graph is a directed acyclic graph with nodes 0 through n-1.
Return every path from node 0 to node n-1.
hints: In a DAG, depth-first search can enumerate paths without cycle handling.
Carry the current path and branch once per outgoing edge.
At target append path; otherwise recurse on each neighbor with path+[neighbor].
Each recursion branch corresponds to one unique edge sequence, so every source-target path is emitted once.
editorial: Each recursion branch corresponds to one unique edge sequence, so every source-target path is emitted once.

tests.explanation: Depth-first traversal finds all five source-to-target routes.
